claims.text: The official Bharatgas transfer form provides Type A transfer by subscriber to family member, Type B outside-family transfer, Type C transfer without transferor consent, Type D next-of-kin transfer after death, and Type E regularization where equipment is held without the subscription voucher.
claims.notes: A form option is not an approval or an indication that a particular case qualifies. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: Bharatgas's public manual says that when a customer shifts within the operating area of the same distributor, the customer should advise the distributor of the new address with supporting residence proof so the distributor changes its records and future supplies go to the new address.
claims.notes: Manual is dated April 2021; current distributor practice and accepted proof list are unknown. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: For a move within the same town where the present distributor does not service the new address, the manual says to approach the old distributor with the original Subscription Voucher for a Transfer Termination Voucher/City Transfer Advise Out, then approach the new distributor with residence proof, TTV/CTA Out and DGCC booklet; the new distributor prepares TSV/CTA In and provides a new consumer number.
claims.notes: This is a published OMC workflow, not an observed Bengaluru transaction. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: The official transfer form requires the transferee to be an Indian citizen above 18, submit documents required by the distributor and deposit equipment security under the distributor's terms; it also declares no existing PSU OMC domestic LPG connection in the same household and an independent household/kitchen.
claims.notes: The form does not provide a universal current document checklist or case-specific fee. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: Bharatgas's customer declaration says that whenever a customer changes residence, the LPG distributor is to be informed in writing in advance so the address can be updated in records.
claims.notes: Declaration is a standard customer undertaking, not evidence that an online transfer route is available. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: No reviewed official public source establishes the current Bengaluru OMC/distributor for a supplied address, current transfer fee/security amount, accepted proof variants, inter-town route, processing status, or whether a particular transfer will be approved.
claims.notes: No login, OTP, connection number, distributor lookup, upload, payment, or submission was performed.

claims.text: The published path branches on whether the new address remains in the same distributor's operating area; if not, the manual describes a same-town transfer using old- and new-distributor voucher steps.
claims.notes: No current Bengaluru service-area check was made. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: For the same distributor area, Bharatgas says to advise the distributor of the new address with supporting residence proof, after which the distributor changes records for future supplies.
claims.notes: Address proof variant and processing result are unobserved. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: For same-town service-area change, the manual says old distributor uses the original Subscription Voucher to prepare TTV/CTA Out; the customer then presents residence proof, TTV/CTA Out and DGCC booklet to the receiving distributor, which prepares TSV/CTA In and provides a new consumer number.
claims.notes: Published 2021 sequence, not a live transaction. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: The blank official form asks for transferor/transferee, SV and consumer number, transfer type and declarations; it includes a distributor physical-verification block.
claims.notes: The form was read only; no personal information or signature was supplied. The original official endpoint is currently unavailable; this claim is retained as incomplete historical/public evidence, not a current complete procedure.

claims.text: No public workflow review establishes the current OMC/distributor for a Bengaluru address, current fee/security deposit, inter-town route, accepted proof variants, or approval/timing for a real connection.
claims.notes: No login, OTP, lookup, upload, payment or submission.

claims.text: One citizen reported completing an online Indane transfer between distributors after moving within Bengaluru.
claims.notes: A single 2016 account. It does not show that the channel still exists, that another OMC uses it, or that any current transfer can complete online.

claims.text: One citizen moving within Bengaluru reported that changing a Bharatgas connection was a difficult experience involving the franchisee.
claims.notes: A single 2011 report of friction. It conflicts with the reported online success only as to lived experience, not as to a universal rule or current service level.

claims.text: The citizen accounts do not establish the current OMC-specific transfer route, service-area determination, accepted proof variants, charge, timing, or delivery result for a Bengaluru connection.
claims.notes: The available accounts are historical and case-specific; no login, transfer, lookup, payment, or personal data was used in this pass.

claims.text: IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that when a customer shifts within the same distributor's operating area, the customer should advise the distributor of the new address with supporting residence proof so the distributor changes its records and future supplies go to the new residence.
claims.notes: Carrier-specific public guidance. It does not identify the assigned Bengaluru distributor or guarantee acceptance of a supplied proof document.

claims.text: IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that for a same-town move outside the present distributor's service area, the old distributor prepares a TTV against the original SV, and the receiving distributor uses proof of residence, TTV and DGCC booklet to prepare a TSV and provide a new consumer number.
claims.notes: IndianOil terminology and sequence only; do not substitute HP Gas e-CTA or BPCL portability language. The FAQ is not a live Bengaluru transaction.

claims.text: IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that an out-of-town move requires surrender of the cylinder and regulator to the current distributor, who prepares a TV and refunds the equipment deposit; the customer is directed to a distributor at the new place for future service.
claims.notes: Carrier-specific published guidance; no equipment was surrendered and no refund or destination distributor was observed.

claims.text: HP Gas's current FAQ says that for a transfer within the city or certain adjoining city, the existing distributor issues an e-CTA/authorisation code against the SV, the e-CTA is valid for three months, and the customer presents the SV and code to the new distributor; cylinder and regulator need not be surrendered.
claims.notes: HPCL's carrier-specific rule. It is not evidence that another OMC uses e-CTA or that a supplied address is within the relevant city/market.

claims.text: HP Gas's current FAQ says that for an out-of-town transfer, the current distributor issues a TV and refunds the SV deposit after surrender of cylinders and regulator; the TV is valid for one year, and the Domestic Gas Consumer Card should be retained for endorsement at the new location.
claims.notes: HPCL carrier guidance; no surrender, TV, refund, endorsement or reconnection was attempted.

claims.text: HP Gas's current FAQ says KYC is required in cases including transfer of connection and change of name after the connection holder's death.
claims.notes: The FAQ does not establish a universal current proof list for every transfer case; no KYC was submitted.

claims.text: HPCL's public LPG systemic-improvements page says its portability feature can transfer an HP Gas connection to another distributor when the consumer changes residence within the city or is dissatisfied with the current distributor, and that requests can only be logged through the HP Gas Consumer Portal or HPPAY with OTP validation.
claims.notes: Current HPCL carrier description. The login/OTP boundary was recorded without attempting authentication.

claims.text: The current Bharatgas portability page says consumers may choose a nearby distributor or change distributor for service dissatisfaction only under a scheme available in selected cities, with no transfer fee or additional security deposit, and that login with a user ID and password is required.
claims.notes: Current BPCL page does not identify the selected-city list or establish that Bengaluru is enabled; no login or request was attempted.

claims.text: The Bharatgas customer declaration says that whenever the customer changes residence, the LPG distributor is to be informed in writing in advance for change of address in the records.
claims.notes: A Bharatgas customer undertaking, not a universal rule for IndianOil or HP Gas and not proof that a written request will be accepted in a particular case.

claims.text: The Bharatgas customer declaration says the customer encloses a completed KYC form with proof of address and proof of identity and accepts household/de-duplication conditions for a domestic subsidized connection.
claims.notes: The declaration does not provide a case-specific current checklist or approval decision; no identity or address data was supplied.

claims.text: The official Bharatgas unified transfer/regularization form lists Type A family transfer, Type B outside-family transfer, Type C transfer without transferor consent, Type D next-of-kin transfer after death and Type E regularization where equipment is held without the subscription voucher.
claims.notes: Blank BPCL form categories are published form content; they do not establish eligibility, distributor acceptance, fee or approval. This is a Bharatgas form observation, not a universal or government requirement.

claims.text: A Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas PIB release dated 2021-06-10 lists OMC portals and mobile apps as channels for LPG portability, transfer of connection and address change for Indane, Bharatgas and HP Gas.
claims.notes: Government policy/public communication, not a current carrier page. Current OMC implementation and Bengaluru availability remain carrier-specific. Dated government communication about OMC services, not a current Bengaluru transaction rule.

claims.text: The same 2021 Ministry/PIB release says online portability lets a customer using a registered login choose a distributor from the list serving the customer's area, and that the facility is free of transfer charges.
claims.notes: This is dated Ministry policy context and should not override a carrier's current selected-city, login, OTP or service-area constraints. Dated government communication about OMC services, not a current Bengaluru transaction rule.

claims.text: The same 2021 Ministry/PIB release says the source distributor may contact the customer and the portability request may be withdrawn within three days; otherwise the connection transfers automatically to the target distributor.
claims.notes: Dated government release; no current portal timer, withdrawal control or automatic transfer was observed. Dated government communication about OMC services, not a current Bengaluru transaction rule.

claims.text: The reviewed official material does not establish the current OMC/distributor assigned to a particular Bengaluru address, whether that address is inside a chosen distributor's service area or portability cluster, the accepted proof variant for a case, a current transfer fee/security amount for every branch, or approval/timing for a supplied connection.
claims.notes: No login, OTP, distributor lookup, upload, payment, equipment handoff or submission was performed.

claims.text: Bharatgas publicly describes LPG connection portability as available in selected cities and says no transfer fee or additional security deposit is charged for that option.
claims.notes: The page does not establish that Bengaluru is currently included or that a particular connection qualifies.

claims.text: Bharatgas's public portability lead sends the user to a login page requiring login ID, password and CAPTCHA before the portability route can be entered.
claims.notes: No login, CAPTCHA, OTP or account information was supplied.

claims.text: Bharatgas exposes a public distributor locator with state and district selectors, but no distributor or service-area result is established without selecting a location.
claims.notes: No Bengaluru state/district selection or distributor lookup was made.

claims.text: Bharatgas's public downloads section lists a unified form for LPG connection transfer or regularization.
claims.notes: The listing and blank form are not evidence of approval, current case eligibility or a completed submission.

claims.text: IndianOil's current public FAQ describes three Indane branches: same distributor area uses new-address proof for a record change; same-town transfer uses SV, TTV, DGCC and TSV without equipment surrender; out-of-town transfer uses SV/TSV and DGCC with equipment surrender for a TV and later reconnection.
claims.notes: Published FAQ sequence only; no Bengaluru distributor, document variant, account state or real transfer result was checked.

claims.text: HPCL's current public FAQ describes within-city or adjoining-city transfer using an e-CTA authorization code with SV and new-distributor enrollment, while an outside-town transfer uses a TV, equipment surrender/refund and reconnection at the new place.
claims.notes: The FAQ is HP Gas-specific and does not establish the route for Bharatgas or Indane.

claims.text: HPCL publicly says its portability option can cover an in-city residence change or dissatisfaction with the current distributor, but the request is initiated through HP Gas portal or HPPAY user login and validated by OTP.
claims.notes: No HP login, OTP or portability request was attempted.

claims.text: This public pass does not establish the current OMC, assigned Bengaluru distributor, service-area match, accepted proof variant, account-specific eligibility, fee other than Bharatgas's portability statement, processing status, approval, consumer-number change or delivery result for any real connection.
claims.notes: The reviewed official routes stop at public guidance, selectors, forms or authenticated boundaries. No login, OTP, lookup, upload, payment or submission occurred.

claims.text: One citizen seeking an LPG address update reported repeatedly finding the assigned agency office closed and being unable to reach the referred regional telephone contact, leaving the update unresolved at the time of posting.
claims.notes: One 2022 account of access and contact friction. It does not establish whether the office was permanently closed, whether another authorised channel was available, the accepted proof, or any current provider practice.

claims.text: One citizen who reported completing an online Indane distributor transfer within Bengaluru also reported being unable to download the transfer document until using the site's feedback channel; they later reported that the download issue was resolved after contact from the service.
claims.notes: One 2016, carrier-specific account. The reported feedback route and recovery are only a historical recovery lead; neither proves a current online route nor a transfer-document requirement for other cases.

claims.text: One citizen reported that, after transferring a Bharatgas connection to Bengaluru, the delivery worker requested an additional payment at delivery and that negotiation did not resolve the request.
claims.notes: One 2026 report of a post-transfer delivery interaction. It does not establish an official or unofficial charge, a provider responsibility, delivery eligibility, a complaint result, or a system-wide practice.

claims.text: The retained citizen accounts do not establish a current OMC-specific address-update or distributor-transfer route, service-area decision, proof acceptance, transfer-document requirement, charge, or delivery outcome in Bengaluru.
claims.notes: The accounts are dated, carrier- and case-specific. Their different channel experiences are not treated as a contradiction because they concern different dates and facts. No authenticated account, application, payment, or personal data was used.

roadblocks.title: OMC/distributor service-area boundary
roadblocks.symptom: A move may be within the old distributor's area, within the same town but another distributor, or outside the town.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Current distributor assignment and area coverage are case-specific.
roadblocks.recovery: Confirm OMC, old distributor, new address and receiving distributor before selecting same-area versus voucher transfer.

roadblocks.title: Case-specific proof and physical verification
roadblocks.symptom: The sources name proof classes and a verification block but do not provide a current universal Bengaluru checklist.
roadblocks.likelyCause: OMC, transfer type, household/de-duplication and distributor practice affect requirements.
roadblocks.recovery: Use the selected OMC's current form and distributor instructions; do not upload or submit in research mode.

roadblocks.title: Service-area branch is case-specific
roadblocks.symptom: New address may or may not be serviced by the current distributor.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Distributor coverage and OMC are not known.
roadblocks.recovery: Confirm current and receiving distributor before acting; no lookup was performed.

roadblocks.title: Processing result unobserved
roadblocks.symptom: No voucher, updated record, new consumer number, payment, inspection or future delivery result exists.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Those states require a real distributor transaction.
roadblocks.recovery: Retain any distributor reference after an authorised transfer; verify current fees and timing with the distributor.

roadblocks.title: Reported transfer channel varies by case
roadblocks.symptom: One historical account reports an online intra-city transfer, while another reports a difficult franchisee interaction.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Unknown; the accounts differ by OMC, date, distributor and possibly service-area facts.
roadblocks.recovery: Use the reports only to confirm the assigned OMC/distributor's current authorised route before relying on a channel or historical experience.

roadblocks.title: Carrier and service-area boundary is case-specific
